verdicts.reason: Both demote the logo from its prominent top-centre badge to a tiny seal jammed in the bottom-left corner. Both blow the legal line up to nearly body-copy size, so the fine print competes with the subhead, and both inflate the CTA into an oversized slab. B is slightly worse: its headline runs almost edge to edge with thin side margins, its legal copy breaks badly and leaves an orphaned 'opening.', and its logo sits even tighter against the canvas corner. A's 'of opening.' wrap is also awkward, but its margins are a little more comfortable.
